A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiSD research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Craftax and Minecraft segmentation and hierarchy results, downstream reinforcement-learning curves, and appendix ablations and classifier evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds an action-labelled demonstration-budget study in Appendix C.3, Table 14.

M1.justification: ASOT segmentation, boundary-constrained Sequitur induction, and BC/PU/PPO deployment remain unchanged. V2 expands their mathematical description and clarifies modularity. Adaptive skill counts and probabilistic grammars are proposed as future work, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Craftax configurations, Minecraft All/Mapped data, and Wooden Pickaxe and Collect Log deployment tasks. Appendix C.3 varies demonstration counts within the existing Craftax task without introducing new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a ground-truth skills-only control to the reported Craftax RL comparisons. Figure 5 also displays CompILE Skills-Only results, although CompILE was already named in v1 Section 7.1. The segmentation comparator set remains CompILE and OMPN.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.3 evaluates 15 BC/PU demonstration budgets from 10 to 500 episodes, fixes PPO training at 100k environment steps, and averages rewards over the final 10%. Appendix E also revises OMPN's reported slot search from {2,3,4,5} to {2,3,4,5,6}; six slots already appeared among v1's selected settings, so this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a focused sensitivity study testing how action-label availability affects flat-skill and hierarchical deployment on Craftax Wooden Pickaxe. The existing K-sensitivity ablation and qualitative skill and hierarchy case studies are retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly discloses that the retained K-sensitivity results use a single random seed (Table 15, formerly Table 13); it does not report a reduction in runs. The new label-budget study specifies 10 PPO seeds and mean ±1 SD. Existing main-table confidence intervals and RL uncertainty conventions remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The main segmentation and hierarchy tables remain numerically unchanged (v1 Tables 1–2; v2 Tables 2–3). Figure 5 adds CompILE rewards of roughly 0.7 and revises the plotted OMPN curve. New Table 14 reports budget-dependent results, including HiSD Hierarchy reward 0.94 ±0.08 at N=250 and zero reward for all four configurations at N=50.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds explicit definitions of the frame-side and skill-side cost matrices and the temporal regularizer in Equations 2–3, where v1 only named the regularization component. Section 2.2 also corrects Sequitur's input description to terminal symbols only. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: observation-only skill discovery combining temporal segmentation with grammar induction, meaningful reusable hierarchies, and downstream RL benefits. The additional deployment evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds the limitation concerning concurrent behaviours under single-skill assignments, concrete future alternatives for choosing K and handling noise, and a contextual explanation of perceptual aliasing. Appendix C.3 interprets low-label failures through compounded BC errors and sample complexity. Deterministic grammar sensitivity to segmentation noise was already discussed in v1 Section 6.2.2.

D1.justification: V2 adds code-availability statements and a GitHub link in the introduction footnote and appendix, clarifies ASOT parameter meanings, and documents the new label-budget experiment. Existing architectures, hardware descriptions, and final selected hyperparameters are retained. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds SloTTAr (Gopalakrishnan et al., 2023) to related work, contrasting its action reconstruction and flat segmentation with HiSD. Lari and Young (1990) and O'Donnell et al. (2009) are added for probabilistic and fragment-grammar future directions. Other reference changes largely update metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites clarifying supervision, segmentation, and result descriptions, standardizes terminology and spelling, and corrects cross-references. It adds Appendix C.3, acknowledgements, and an impact statement, and changes author order and publication-header text. The overall section sequence and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the supervision-summary Table 1 and label-budget Table 14. Figure 5 gains the CompILE curve and an expanded legend; Figures 5–6 receive axis-label and caption edits, including corrected colour references. Existing displays are largely retained, with relocation and localized layout changes such as stacking Figures 3–4.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens deployment evidence with the label-budget study and displayed CompILE results, while improving mathematical clarity, code-access information, statistical disclosure, and limitations. These are useful, bounded gains: the method and core benchmark tables remain unchanged, and the new label-efficiency evidence covers one Craftax task with substantial non-monotonicity and occasional collapse at smaller budgets.
